caption: Figure 1. Matrix–vector multiply with analog PUM.
subject: how an analog PUM crossbar performs a 2x2 matrix by 2x1 vector multiply via conductances, row voltages, and column currents

groups.why_chosen: An analog crossbar reproduces a matrix-vector multiply physically: matrix values become programmed conductances, input-vector values become row voltages, Ohm's law multiplies them at each junction, and Kirchhoff's current law accumulates the products down each column into the result.
groups.what_to_learn: a plain arithmetic panel paired with a physically-realized circuit panel computing the same worked example; consistent per-value colour coding carried from a circuit diagram into the arithmetic equations that verify it; circled step numbers overlaid on a crossbar to narrate program -> multiply -> accumulate -> result
